mt-0i5u.title: Plate: EU blue strip, often short
mt-0i5u.summary: Plates have the blue strip on the left like most of Europe, but short, almost square plates are very common here.

mt-4s8H.title: Houses: low, white to beige walls
mt-4s8H.summary: Most buildings are low, with white to beige walls. Limestone-built houses are also fairly common.

mt-A85X.title: Walls: pale limestone rock walls
mt-A85X.summary: Low walls made of stacked pale limestone rock line the fields and roads. This alone is usually enough to tell you it is Malta.

mt-CXV5.title: Sign: blue signs unique to the capital
mt-CXV5.summary: These blue signs are only found in the capital, Valletta, so seeing one tells you where on the island you are.

mt-CkGF.title: Sign: street name with "triq"
mt-CkGF.summary: The word "triq" means street and appears on almost every street name sign.

mt-LOnP.title: Guardrail: low stone barriers instead
mt-LOnP.summary: On the small island of Gozo, normal metal guardrails are rare. Low stone barriers line the roads instead.

mt-S9ac.title: Road lines: double yellow no-parking lines
mt-S9ac.summary: Two yellow lines along the kerb mean no parking, as in the UK and Ireland. With left-hand driving, that narrows it to those countries or Malta.

mt-XUts.title: Language: Maltese letters Ċ Ġ Ħ Ż
mt-XUts.summary: Maltese uses Latin letters plus special ones with dots or bars: Ċ, Ġ, Ħ and Ż. It is related to Arabic but has many Italian words.

mt-ZuPI.title: Landscape: dry fields, cacti, narrow roads
mt-ZuPI.summary: Gently hilly, dry farm fields with cacti and dry shrubs. Many roads are only one or two lanes wide because the island is small.

mt-aUAp.title: Coverage: backpack shots on a white-blue ferry
mt-aUAp.summary: The coverage taken on a white and blue ship crosses between the main island and Gozo.

mt-eHEp.title: Language: English is everywhere
mt-eHEp.summary: English is the main language, so you will see lots of English signs and shop names.

mt-rb2X.title: Bus routes: numbers in the 300s
mt-rb2X.summary: Every bus route on Gozo has a number in the 300s. They are hard to spot, so they mostly help in games where you can move.

mt-v6Vj.title: Bus stops: common, with local info
mt-v6Vj.summary: Bus stops are everywhere on the islands. They sometimes show useful information, like route numbers or place names, that tells you where you are.

mt-vABj.title: Driving side: left
mt-vABj.summary: Cars drive on the left. Cyprus also drives on the left, so this narrows it to Malta or Cyprus.

mt-xVAC.title: Houses: covered wooden balconies
mt-xVAC.summary: Traditional enclosed balconies stick out from the walls of many buildings. They are often painted in bright colours.
